title: What the Operator Asks For: A Velocity Command, Clipped to What the Robot Can Do and Eased Toward by a Bounded Acceleration

questions.question: Why is the limit on forward and sideways speed an ellipse?
options: Each motor has its own speed limit, and an ellipse is the sum of the four
The body is longer than it is wide, so it has more inertia about one axis
An ellipse is cheaper to compute than a rectangle on a small processor
A leg can step further forward than sideways, so the two are limited together
questions.explanation: The limit comes from the legs' reach, which is longer fore and aft than to the side. A rectangle would allow the full forward and the full sideways speed at once, a diagonal that asks for a step no leg can take.

questions.question: A command of 1.0 forward and 0.4 sideways became:
options: 1.0 and 0.4, unchanged, because each is within its own limit
1.0 and 0.0, the sideways part dropped to keep the forward speed
0.71 and 0.28, the same direction
0.50 and 0.20, each halved
questions.explanation: The command sits at the corner of the rectangle, which is outside the ellipse by a factor of the square root of two. Both parts are divided by that, so the direction is kept: 0.71 and 0.28.

questions.question: A jump to 0.8 m/s took how long?
options: 0.40 s, since the ramp starts from half way
1.60 s, there and back
One time step: the limit only applies to the turn rate
questions.explanation: The command in use may change by at most 1.0 m/s in each second, so 0.8 m/s takes 0.80 s. It is the same going down as going up.

questions.question: The legs allowed what top speed?
options: 0.80 m/s: a 0.20 m step over a 0.25 s stance
1.0 m/s, the limit set on the stick
2.0 m/s, which needed a step within reach
questions.explanation: The fastest speed is the longest step over the shortest stance time: 0.20 m over 0.125 s. At 2.0 m/s the step needed was beyond the leg's reach.

questions.question: What does a jump in the command do to the legs?
options: Tells the body to be where it is not, and the feet cannot follow
Makes the servos overheat at once, before the body has moved
Changes the gait from a trot to a walk without a transition
Nothing: the leg controller filters it out on its own
questions.explanation: The gaits of phase 35 plan each step from the commanded velocity. A velocity that jumps asks for a body position the feet were not placed for, so the command is eased and not handed on as it comes.

questions.question: What sets the top speed limit?
options: The longest step over the shortest stance, from the legs
The limit on the stick, chosen by the operator
The battery's voltage under load
The ellipse, which is drawn first and the legs made to fit it
questions.explanation: The legs decide: reach and the quickest swing the servos can do. The limit on the command has to be set below that, however far the stick is pushed.
